item.title: Central Bank independence in today’s world - Speech by Andrew Bailey

rating.summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey delivered a broad lecture at Zurich University covering three themes: the importance of central bank independence in a shock-prone world, the inseparability of monetary and financial stability mandates, and the financial stability risks and opportunities posed by AI. The speech contains only brief, high-level references to monetary policy with no forward guidance on interest rates or the policy outlook. The primary focus is on institutional legitimacy, financial regulation, and AI-related risks.
rating.stance_rationale: The speech is largely philosophical and institutional in nature rather than a monetary policy statement; there is no meaningful rate guidance, inflation outlook, or easing/tightening bias expressed, making a monetary policy score inappropriate.
key_quotes: Our task is to set interest rates to bring inflation back to target.
Sustained economic growth depends on financial stability.
